metaDescription: Zelienople, Butler County mineral owner? We buy Marcellus interests directly, walk through your royalty statement, and close on your schedule.
heroLead: Zelienople is one of the more established boroughs in Butler County, and the mineral ownership underneath it reflects a mix of longtime family land and newer suburban development.
intro: Zelienople has grown a lot over the years, and that growth has changed the character of the land above the mineral estate even as the ownership underneath often stayed with the same families who held it before the subdivisions arrived. If you're one of those owners, your mineral rights might be the last piece of the original farm your family kept.
We understand what that kind of holding means to a family, and we don't treat it like just another line item.

sections.heading: Suburban Growth, Rural Ownership
paragraphs: As Zelienople and the surrounding area have developed, a lot of the original farm tracts got subdivided for housing while the mineral rights stayed intact and separate, sometimes owned by descendants who no longer live anywhere near the property. Tracking down exactly which subdivided parcels still connect back to the original mineral estate takes real title work.
We do that work through the Butler County recorder of deeds before making any offer, so the number we give you reflects a confirmed interest, not an estimate.

sections.heading: What Butler County Leasing Has Looked Like
paragraphs: Butler County saw a mix of independent and major operators active over the years, with development generally steadier and less concentrated than the wet gas core counties to the south. Zelienople-area interests can vary widely in production depending on the specific unit and how recently it was developed.
We pull your actual production history rather than relying on general assumptions about the county.

sections.heading: Explaining the Numbers Without the Runaround
paragraphs: If reading your royalty statement feels like decoding a foreign language, gathering fees, marketing deductions, decimal interests, you're not alone. We'll walk through it with you in plain terms before any offer gets discussed.

faqs.question: My family's land near Zelienople was subdivided for housing. Do we still own the minerals?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. Mineral rights frequently stay with the original owner or their heirs even after the surface is subdivided and sold for development. We confirm this through county deed records.

faqs.question: How active is Marcellus drilling in this part of Butler County?
faqs.answer: Development has been steadier and more moderate here than in the wet gas core counties further south. We evaluate your specific unit's production before making an offer.

faqs.question: What if I'm not sure whether my family retained the mineral rights?
faqs.answer: We can research that for you through the Butler County recorder of deeds as part of our review, at no cost.
